source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 189: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer:
Decision framework and assumptions: choose tensor parallelism (TP) when the model must be split within layers and the GPUs have sufficiently fast, predictable interconnects; choose pipeline parallelism (PP) when contiguous layer stages fit each GPU and avoiding frequent intra-layer collectives matters. Freeze model revision, tokenizer, precision, kernel/runtime versions, GPU count and types, topology, request mix, context/output distributions, concurrency, SLOs, and fault budget. Account for embeddings/LM head replication, serving buffers, KV-cache placement, workspace peaks, and uneven stage sizes; do not claim a universal winner without measurements.

Falsifiable hypothesis: for this latency-sensitive workload, the selected scheme meets predeclared p50 and p99 end-to-end latency and throughput targets, stays below a per-GPU memory watermark, and preserves output correctness. TP predicts that measured collective time and synchronization overhead are lower than PP transfer plus pipeline-bubble cost; PP predicts the reverse. Falsify the choice if any SLO, memory, or correctness gate fails, or if recovery exceeds the fault budget.

Controlled experiment: build semantically equivalent TP and PP variants from the same frozen artifact. Run identical seeded, stratified request traces covering prompt/output lengths and concurrency, with warmup followed by randomized repeated trials. Measure TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end p50/p95/p99, completed tokens/s, queueing, per-layer collective or stage-transfer time, utilization, per-GPU peak allocated/reserved memory, KV-cache occupancy, and errors, all with units and synchronized timestamps. Sweep microbatch size and PP schedule, and sweep feasible TP degree; report confidence intervals and paired differences. Verify logits/output equivalence within an agreed tolerance and test saturation separately from the latency target.

Control confounders including thermal state, clocks, placement, NUMA/network path, software versions, background load, cache/warmup state, admission limits, and run order. Isolate prefill from decode and distinguish measured facts from estimates. Canary the winner at bounded concurrency and traffic, preserve the prior configuration, and roll back on SLO/correctness/memory breaches, error spikes, or failed health checks. Exercise worker loss, stage timeout, collective timeout, and reconfiguration with finite timeouts; require fencing, no split brain, bounded restart/reload, and documented data-loss/retry behavior before asserting fault tolerance. Evidence remains provisional until topology, traces, repeated measurements, correctness checks, and failure-injection results are collected.

quality_dimensions.safety: bounded canary, correctness checks, finite timeouts, and rollback

source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 298: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer:
Decision framework and assumptions: choose tensor parallelism (TP) when the model must be split within layers and the GPUs have sufficiently fast, predictable interconnects; choose pipeline parallelism (PP) when contiguous layer stages fit each GPU and avoiding frequent intra-layer collectives matters. Freeze model revision, tokenizer, precision, kernel/runtime versions, GPU count and types, topology, request mix, context/output distributions, concurrency, SLOs, and fault budget. Account for embeddings/LM head replication, serving buffers, KV-cache placement, workspace peaks, and uneven stage sizes; do not claim a universal winner without measurements.

Falsifiable hypothesis: for this latency-sensitive workload, the selected scheme meets predeclared p50 and p99 end-to-end latency and throughput targets, stays below a per-GPU memory watermark, and preserves output correctness. TP predicts that measured collective time and synchronization overhead are lower than PP transfer plus pipeline-bubble cost; PP predicts the reverse. Falsify the choice if any SLO, memory, or correctness gate fails, or if recovery exceeds the fault budget.

Controlled experiment: build semantically equivalent TP and PP variants from the same frozen artifact. Run identical seeded, stratified request traces covering prompt/output lengths and concurrency, with warmup followed by randomized repeated trials. Measure TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end p50/p95/p99, completed tokens/s, queueing, per-layer collective or stage-transfer time, utilization, per-GPU peak allocated/reserved memory, KV-cache occupancy, and errors, all with units and synchronized timestamps. Sweep microbatch size and PP schedule, and sweep feasible TP degree; report confidence intervals and paired differences. Verify logits/output equivalence within an agreed tolerance and test saturation separately from the latency target.

Control confounders including thermal state, clocks, placement, NUMA/network path, software versions, background load, cache/warmup state, admission limits, and run order. Isolate prefill from decode and distinguish measured facts from estimates. Canary the winner at bounded concurrency and traffic, preserve the prior configuration, and roll back on SLO/correctness/memory breaches, error spikes, or failed health checks. Exercise worker loss, stage timeout, collective timeout, and reconfiguration with finite timeouts; require fencing, no split brain, bounded restart/reload, and documented data-loss/retry behavior before asserting fault tolerance. Evidence remains provisional until topology, traces, repeated measurements, correctness checks, and failure-injection results are collected.
